# UK Tax Deadlines & Penalties (2026/27)

## Corporation Tax

### CT600 Return
- **Filing deadline**: 12 months after the end of the accounting period
- **Payment deadline**: 9 months and 1 day after the accounting period ends — earlier than the filing deadline
- **Example**: year-end 31 March 2026 → pay by 1 January 2027, file by 31 March 2027
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/company-tax-returns/penalties-for-late-filing>

### Late Filing Penalties (CT600)
| Delay | Penalty |
|-------|---------|
| 1 day late | £100 |
| 3 months late | Additional £100 |
| 6 months late | HMRC estimates tax owed + 10% of unpaid tax |
| 12 months late | Additional 10% of unpaid tax |

- If the return is late two years running, the £100 penalties increase to **£500** each
- Interest accrues on late payments from the due date

### Large Company Instalments
- Companies with profits over £1.5 million must pay in quarterly instalments
- Due in months 7, 10, 13, and 16 of the accounting period
- Very large companies (profits over £20 million) pay in months 3, 6, 9, and 12

## Annual Accounts (Companies House)

### Filing Deadline
- **Private company**: 9 months after the financial year-end
- **Public company (PLC)**: 6 months after the financial year-end
- **First accounts**: 21 months from date of incorporation

### Late Filing Penalties (Private Company)
| Delay | Penalty |
|-------|---------|
| Up to 1 month | £150 |
| 1-3 months | £375 |
| 3-6 months | £750 |
| Over 6 months | £1,500 |

- **Penalties double** if accounts are late two years in a row
- Companies House will not accept "I didn't know" as an excuse
- Directors are personally responsible for ensuring timely filing
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/annual-accounts/penalties-for-late-filing>

## Confirmation Statement

- **Frequency**: at least once every 12 months from incorporation or the last filing
- **Filing deadline**: within 14 days of the review date
- **Filing fee**: **£34 online, £62 paper** (raised from £13 in May 2024)
- **Penalty for non-filing**: criminal offence — directors can be prosecuted; company can be struck off
- Confirms company details are up to date: registered office, directors, shareholders, SIC codes, PSC register
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/file-your-confirmation-statement-with-companies-house>

## VAT Returns

### Standard Quarterly
- Due: **1 month and 7 days** after the end of the VAT quarter
- Must file via MTD-compatible software (mandatory since April 2022 for all VAT-registered businesses)

### Late Filing (Points-Based System — from Jan 2023)
- 1 point per late submission
- Penalty threshold:
  - Annual returns: 2 points
  - Quarterly returns: 4 points
  - Monthly returns: 5 points
- Once threshold reached: **£200 per late return**
- Points expire after 24 months of timely submissions

### Late Payment
| Delay | Penalty |
|-------|---------|
| Up to 15 days | No penalty (interest still accrues) |
| 16-30 days | 2% of outstanding VAT |
| 31+ days | 2% + further 2% of amount still outstanding |
| Ongoing | Daily interest at Bank of England base rate + 2.5% |

## PAYE / Payroll

### Monthly RTI Submissions
- **Full Payment Submission (FPS)**: on or before each payday
- **Employer Payment Summary (EPS)**: by 19th of the following month (e.g. if no employees paid)
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/running-payroll/reporting-to-hmrc>

### PAYE Payment
- Due: 22nd of the month following the tax month (electronic) or 19th (cheque)
- Quarterly payments available for small employers (under £1,500/month average)

### P11D (Benefits in Kind)
- Filing deadline: **6 July** following the end of the tax year
- Class 1A NIC payment: **22 July** (electronic)

### Late RTI Penalties
| Number of Defaults in tax year | Penalty (% of amount due) |
|---|---|
| 1st late payment | No penalty |
| 2nd-3rd | 1% |
| 4th-6th | 2% |
| 7th-9th | 3% |
| 10+ | 4% |
| 6+ months late | Additional 5% of outstanding amount |
| 12+ months late | Further 5% |

## Self Assessment

- **Registration**: by 5 October following the tax year (for first-time filers)
- **Paper return**: 31 October following the tax year
- **Online return**: 31 January following the tax year
- **Payments on Account**: due 31 January and 31 July (50% each) — required if previous SA bill > £1,000 AND less than 80% collected at source
- **Balancing payment**: 31 January following the tax year
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/self-assessment-tax-returns/deadlines>

### Late Filing Penalties
| Delay | Penalty |
|-------|---------|
| 1 day late | £100 (immediate) |
| 3 months late | £10/day for up to 90 days (max £900) |
| 6 months late | Greater of £300 or 5% of tax due |
| 12 months late | Greater of £300 or 5% of tax due (up to 100% in serious cases) |

## MTD for Income Tax — NEW 2026/27

- **Now mandatory** for sole traders and landlords with gross income over £50,000 (from 6 April 2026)
- Quarterly submission deadlines: Q1 due **7 Aug**, Q2 due **7 Nov**, Q3 due **7 Feb**, Q4 due **7 May**
- Final Declaration due 31 January after tax year end
- April 2027: extends to those over £30,000 income
- April 2028: expected to extend to those over £20,000 (subject to legislation)

## Annual Compliance Calendar

### April
- Start of new tax year (6 April)
- Submit P60s to employees (by 31 May)
- Review salary/dividend strategy for new year
- New tax year rates take effect

### May-June
- File P11D forms (by 6 July)

### July
- Self Assessment second payment on account (31 July)
- P11D Class 1A NIC payment (22 July)

### August
- First MTD ITSA quarterly submission Q1 (7 Aug — for those mandated)

### September-October
- Most companies' annual accounts deadline (if March year-end)
- Self Assessment paper return deadline (31 October)
- Check all Companies House filings are up to date

### November
- MTD ITSA Q2 due (7 Nov)

### January
- Self Assessment online deadline (31 January)
- SA balancing payment + first POA (31 January)
- Corporation Tax payment for March year-end (1 January)

### February
- MTD ITSA Q3 due (7 Feb)

### Quarterly throughout year
- VAT returns (dates depend on your VAT stagger)
- Review management accounts
- Check cash flow against forecasts
